writtenTo: The Jewish exiles and all believers awaiting God's kingdom
importantNotes: Daniel's prophecies of four world empires (chs. 2, 7) have been remarkably fulfilled.
The fiery furnace and the lions' den are iconic stories of faith under pressure.
Daniel 9:24-27 contains the prophecy of 'seventy weeks' — pointing to the Messiah.
'The Son of Man coming on the clouds' (7:13) is the title Jesus used most for Himself.
Daniel served faithfully under multiple pagan kings — a model of integrity in hostile culture.

chapters.1: Daniel and friends taken to Babylon; they refuse the king's food and are blessed.
chapters.2: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great statue — four world empires and God's eternal kingdom.
chapters.3: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image; they survive the fiery furnace.
chapters.4: Nebuchadnezzar's pride is humbled — he lives as a beast until he acknowledges God.
chapters.5: Belshazzar's feast; the writing on the wall — 'MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN'; Babylon falls.
chapters.6: Daniel in the lions' den — his faithfulness to God and miraculous deliverance.
chapters.7: Daniel's vision of four beasts and the Son of Man — world empires and God's eternal kingdom.
chapters.8: The vision of the ram and goat — Medo-Persia and Greece; Antiochus Epiphanes foreshadowed.
chapters.9: Daniel's prayer of confession; the prophecy of the seventy weeks pointing to the Messiah.
chapters.10: Daniel's vision by the Tigris River; the angel's delayed arrival due to spiritual warfare.
chapters.11: Detailed prophecy of wars between kingdoms of the North and South; the 'king who exalts himself.'
chapters.12: The time of the end — resurrection, judgment, and the sealing of the prophecy.
